newsitem.title: USA: Atmos sees merger costs in Q4, also savings.
newsitem.headline: Atmos sees merger costs in Q4, also savings.

text.p: Atmos Energy Corp said Wednesday it expects its merger with United Cities Gas Co to total about $17 million in transaction costs and $32 million for separation and other costs.
The company, which completed its merger with United Cities on July 31, said it will cut 635 jobs in the next 12 months, including 560 utility positions at United Cities and 75 Atmos positions.
Since a substantial portion of the costs are related to the job cuts and fees payable at the close of the merger, Atmos plans to account for the costs in the fourth quarter, it said.

The company said it expects cost savings from the merger to be about $375 million over the next 10 years, with a significant amount of the costs to be recovered through rates and future operating efficiencies.
The company said it will create a general reserve of about $12.8 million after-tax to account for costs that may not be recovered.
"We will begin to see the positive benefits of these initiatives in 1998, and the full benefits in 1999 and beyond," a company statement said.
Atmos said the merger makes it the twelfth largest natural gas utility in the nation.
Earlier Wednesay Atmos reported net income of $.5 million, or $0.03 per share for the third quarter, compared to $300,000 or $0.02 a share for the third quarter of 1996.
